content:
sam: Heads-up: BrightLeaf (dedicated tenant tb_brightleaf_01) reporting repeated 429s and 2-3s tail latency on long-context generation. Customer says it started ~09:12 UTC, mostly long-context streaming requests. They see failures on ~30% of requests.

brightleaf-support: Confirmed. Calls are to our ded-west-003 endpoint. Example payload attached (context ~65k tokens). We repro locally with a subset — gets intermittent 429 + "kv-cache-evict-throttle" in logs.

tanya: Can you paste pool/node ids and a short log snippet? I want to see eviction pattern and any autoscaler activity.

sam: pool=ded-west-003
nodes: infer-03a, infer-03b (both NVIDIA A10x) ; tenant_id=tb_brightleaf_01

logs snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T09:13:21Z] INFO evicting-kv entries=312 reason=memory_pressure tenant=tb_brightleaf_01
[2026-03-15T09:13:22Z] WARN kv-evict-throttle active=true wait_ms=120
[2026-03-15T09:13:27Z] ERROR serve: request=429 reason=kv-cache-saturated
```

metrics snapshot (09:12-09:16):
```
evictions/sec: 0.5 -> 120 (spike)
kv_cache_used_mb (tenant): 1832 / 2048
node_mem_used_mb: 18240 / 24576
mem_frag_ratio: 1.42
inflight_longctx: 24 (burst -> queueing)
p95_latency: 2.1s
```

leo: Autoscaler shows a scale attempt at 09:14 but it logged "scale-prevented: recently_backoff" and did not add nodes. min=2 max=8 current=2. Autoscaler-bot event below.

autoscaler-bot: scale_event: attempt=2026-03-15T09:14:08Z result=prevented reason=recent_out_of_scale backoff_until=2026-03-15T09:18:08Z

tanya: This looks like KV window bloat: lots of long-context requests create huge KV footprints, causing frequent evictions and fragmentation. Evictions create CPU/IO spikes and the throttle kicks in before autoscaler can react (because mem pressure doesn't trigger scale, and backoff prevented additional nodes). Could be exacerbated by fragmentation (fragmented GPU host memory still tallies as used).

sam: Repro steps we ran (minimal):
1) payload.json (context ~60-70k tokens)
2) for i in {1..30}; do curl -s -X POST https://ded-west-003.redwood.internal/v1/generate \
   -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d @payload.json &
   sleep 0.5
   done
We see evictions start around request 8-10 and 429s increase after ~15 concurrent longctx.

tanya: Quick mitigations we can apply now:
- apply per-tenant concurrency cap for long-context endpoints (soft limit 6)
- enable short-lived per-request KV eviction window (lower cache cap for tenant)
- temporarily bump pool to 4 nodes (manual scale) to give breathing room
I've created a short runbook patch and can push per-tenant cap in 5m.

leo: Created internal incident INC-5478, applied soft concurrency cap=6 to tb_brightleaf_01 (non-blocking 429s replaced with queued 429->503 fallback handled). Also temporarily increased pool node count to 4 (manual add). Monitoring now.

sam: Customer informed and asked for root cause & ETA. They also mentioned billing alarm triggered due to retry storms — want to avoid extra charges.

tanya: Longer term actions / follow-ups:
- add autoscaler rule: treat sustained kv_evictions/sec > 20 as scale-up signal
- introduce fragmentation reclaim job to compact KV pages during low-util windows
- add tenant-level KV quotas and eviction-priorities so a single tenant can't thrash whole node
- add a prewarm path for long-context on Dedicated that reserves persistent KV slots when job starts

leo: Note: billing team suggested also warning customers in-app when their workload exceeds long-context thresholds (prevent surprise). I'll create a ticket for product.

brightleaf-support: Thanks, will advise BrightLeaf to throttle from their side and test with the per-tenant cap. Will report back in 2 hours.

tanya: Monitoring notes: keeping alert on evictions/sec and mem_frag_ratio > 1.3. If p95 latency > 2s or 429s > 5% after 30m, we'll rollback the cap and initiate deeper heap compaction.

sam: Thanks team. :thumbsup: Keep logs and a short timeline in INC-5478. Follow-up meeting at 11:00 UTC if still elevated. :hourglass:
